anomaly_def.Name: SQL Workload Logic Anomaly + Transaction Log Subsystem Anomaly + Storage Space Capacity Anomaly
anomaly_def.Description:
Composite Definition: The database is concurrently affected by (1) SQL Workload Logic Anomaly—application-level statement or transaction patterns that generate excessive or inefficient data manipulation, (2) Transaction Log Subsystem Anomaly—commit-path bottlenecks related to log buffering, flushing, or archival, and (3) Storage Space Capacity Anomaly—approaching or reached hard limits on physical or logical free space for data, log, archive, or temporary areas.

Combined Observable Phenomena: • Statement latency and slow-query frequency rise sharply while commit latency, log-flush waits, and log-sync waits increase in lockstep. • Log files switch more often, archives pile up, and free space in both active log volumes and archive destinations plummets, triggering space-related alerts. • When log segments cannot be recycled because archives lag or space is exhausted, new writes stall, causing application timeouts and long-running transactions to linger even longer, holding locks and further inflating contention. • Auto-extension failures, "out of space" errors, and checkpoint storms occur simultaneously with runaway redo generation and prolonged user transactions, making the symptoms appear as a single, escalating performance and availability incident.

Causal Chain and Interaction: Inefficient SQL patterns (wide scans, over-sized batches, long open transactions) inflate redo volume per transaction. The surging redo stresses the transaction-log subsystem, driving more frequent flushes, switches, and archive operations. Because the storage layer is already at—or near—capacity, log and archive files cannot grow or be archived fast enough, which in turn blocks further log allocation. Blocked log allocation stalls commits, elongates transaction lifetimes, and amplifies the workload logic anomaly’s original resource footprint. The prolonged transactions occupy additional temp and undo/rollback space, accelerating overall space exhaustion. Thus, each root cause reinforces the others: inefficient SQL generates excessive redo; excessive redo overwhelms the log subsystem; the overwhelmed log subsystem consumes and fragments remaining space, and tight storage capacity feeds back to block log processing, creating a self-amplifying degradation loop that jeopardizes OLTP throughput and system availability.

entry.official_definition: The time limit for regular expression matching operations performed by the regular expression engine.
entry.trigger_condition: A regular expression match operation exceeds regexp_time_limit.
entry.workload_impact: The regular expression operation is constrained by the configured time limit.
entry.default_behavior: Defined as a MySQL server system variable.
entry.cause_analysis: This timeout is usually triggered when statement execution exceeds a configured execution-time budget because the operation runs too long or the workload is blocked behind other work.
entry.solution_guidance: Inspect query shape, access path quality, resource contention, and whether the timeout threshold should be reviewed together with the workload pattern.
